newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet approves rubber price hike.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet approves rubber price hike.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday approved a proposal to increase the rubber intervention price to 29 baht ($1.11) a kg from 27.5 baht previously from now until July 31, Deputy Agriculture Minister Krish Kongpetchara said.
Krish told reporters the government would set aside 4.7 billion baht to buy rubber from Thai planters during that period.
Krish said the government could start buying rubber 10 days from now as a committee would be set up to check into methods of buying and on the rubber that is left in stock.

On May 2, Krish signed a memorandum of understanding with disgruntled rubber holders in the south, agreeing to their demands by promising that the government would raise the intervention price to 29.00 baht a kg from 27.50 baht previously.
Last week some ministers raised objections to the plan, saying the protest to demand the hike was engineered by the opposition.
They also said the intervention plan could cost the government of between seven and 10 billion baht.
